This page covers two things that go together: how you find records in your knowledge environment, and how you read what you find — fields, related records, media, citations, and a preview of what a published record looks like to a reader outside your project. Read it when search is not finding what you expect, when you need a scholarly citation from a record, or when you want to check how a record will read before it is published. What is available depends on how your environment is configured. The sections below describe what the platform supports; your project may use all of it or a subset.

Quick search — a search panel that finds records across every collection you can access. Results are grouped by collection and show which fields matched; selecting a result opens the record. Scope it to the current table, to everything you can access, or to a single collection. Maturity: Active. Search & Read — a full search page for browsing, filtering, and reading results in place. Scope the search to a collection and add conditions on field values; the page address encodes your whole search, so it can be shared. Maturity: Active. Current-table filtering — a toolbar box that narrows the rows already loaded in the active table, and a filter builder for column conditions. Maturity: Active. Details panel — every field of a record, including fields the table does not display as columns. A separate Relations view shows the record's connections. Maturity: Active. Reader preview — the Details panel includes a preview pane rendered with the same engine as the public reader, so what you see is what a reader would see. Maturity: Active. Media and citations — a record's reading view lists its attached media, and citations are rendered in your project's citation style (defined in Citation Style Language, the format reference managers like Zotero understand). Maturity: Active. Limit: which media appear depends on what your project attached.

Open quick search from the Search database… control at the top of the workspace, or press Ctrl+Shift+F (⌘⇧F on Mac). Type a term. Results appear grouped by collection, each showing the record's label and the fields where your term matched. Select a result to open that record. The panel starts scoped to Current table when a table is active. Switch to All workspace to search everything you can access, or narrow the search to a single collection. This is the right tool for "find this person, source, or term, wherever it lives." Quick search matches against the fields your environment includes in its search configuration — by default, the text fields of each record. Matching is forgiving about diacritics: in a polytonic-Greek project, a term typed in modern monotonic Greek finds its polytonic spellings — breathings, iota subscripts, and circumflex and grave accents are all ignored — and Arabic vowel marks are ignored the same way. The acute accent and the diaeresis still count, in Greek and in Latin script alike: a term typed with no accents at all can miss a record whose stored form carries one. If your project keeps a native-script field, a transliteration, and a translation side by side, a term in any of them finds the record, provided those fields are searchable. Which fields those are is set by your environment administrator.
documents.s: Quick search — find a record anywhere you can access

documents.t: When you want to look at many records rather than jump to one, open Search & Read: select Open full Search & Read at the bottom of the quick search panel — your typed term carries over — or choose Search & Read from the command palette (Ctrl+K / ⌘K). Search & Read is built for dwelling. Switch to Advanced mode to scope the search to one collection and add conditions on field values — each condition names a field, a match type (contains, equals, or starts with), and a value, and can be negated; conditions combine with Match all or with any. Sort results by relevance, by recently modified, or by label, and page through them. For any result you can expand its full fields inline, open it in a reading pane beside the list, or click through to the record itself. If a collection needs a review access you do not hold, the page tells you how many are hidden rather than failing silently. The page address encodes your query, filters, page, and sort order. Paste the address to a colleague and they see the same results — see Share a search. For a side-by-side comparison of the two search tools, see Choose between the quick search bar and Search & Read.
documents.s: Search & Read — browse, filter, and read in place

documents.t: The table toolbar gives you two ways to narrow what is in front of you: Filter visible rows… — type a term and the table narrows to the loaded rows that contain it, in whichever script the text is written. This box matches text as written in the row; it works on what is already loaded and does not search the rest of the workspace. Filter — opens the filter builder for column conditions. Active filters appear as chips on the toolbar; remove one, or clear them all. You can combine the two — apply column filters, then type in the filter box — or use either alone. Filter-only browsing, with no typed term, is a good way to survey a slice of your corpus.

Click a row to open its Details panel. Every field of the record is shown, including fields the table does not display as columns. Relation fields are marked as such; the Relations view shows the record's connections in one place. Alongside the fields, a Saved reader preview pane renders the record as a reader outside your project would see it — same layout, same fonts, same citations, same media rendering — without making anything public. Read it, spot anything that looks wrong, and fix it in the fields beside it. Public reader covers the full path from draft to published page.

A record's reading view lists its attached media — images, audio, video, or 3D models, whichever your project attached. Each media item is itself a record, with its own description and its own citation. Where a dedicated viewer exists for a media type, the item opens in that viewer. Citations are rendered in your project's citation style and are ready to copy into a bibliography — the same structured form reference managers understand. The same applies to source records: opening one shows a citation you can reuse. How citations are composed and how they appear to outside readers is covered in Public reader.
documents.s: Media and citations on a record

documents.t: Symptom Likely cause Fix Quick search returns nothing for a record you know exists. Your term appears only in a field your environment does not include in its search configuration, or your term is missing an acute accent the stored form carries. Type the term with its accents, or try a word from a different field of the record. If it still does not appear, contact your environment administrator to review which fields are searchable. The search panel reports "Search isn't enabled for this workspace yet." Search has not been switched on for your environment. The toolbar filter box still works on the active table. Contact your environment administrator. A transliterated search misses a record whose native-script form you know is there. The transliteration field is empty on that record, or it is not marked searchable. Try the native-script form. If that succeeds, contact your environment administrator so the transliteration field can be reviewed. The toolbar filter box does not find a record you expect. The box only narrows rows already loaded in the active table; the record may live in another collection. Use quick search instead — it searches every collection you can access. Search results show strings of letters and numbers instead of names. The collection has no display field configured, so results fall back to an internal identifier. Contact your environment administrator and ask them to set a display field for that collection. A citation under a media item looks incomplete or shows placeholders. The citation fields are missing on the media record itself. Open the media record's Details and complete the citation fields. If the field requirements look wrong for your project, contact your environment administrator.

While you work, the platform may show small tips beside the record or the import you are reviewing — short notes about a faster way to do what you are already doing, or about something a record might be missing. Tips are advice, not commands. They never change your data, never block you, and go away on their own once they no longer apply. Read this page if you are wondering why a tip appeared, what to do with it, or why one you expected did not.

Improvement tips in the workspace — when the record you have selected has noticeably fewer filled fields than similar records in your environment, a tip names a field you could add. The comparison needs at least three similar records, and the tip stays silent when there is nothing meaningful to suggest. Maturity: Active. Efficiency tips during import review — when you make the same correction three or more times while reviewing an import, a tip notes the pattern, so you can adjust the rule once instead of correcting every remaining row by hand. Maturity: Active. A panel that stays out of the way — tips appear in a panel beside your work. In the workspace, the most confident tips show directly and the rest wait under a collapsed "More suggestions" heading; during import review, only confident tips appear. When nothing clears the confidence bar, no panel appears at all. Maturity: Active. Environment-wide off switch — your environment administrator can turn tips off for the whole environment; when off, no tips appear anywhere. Maturity: Active. Standardization tips — a third kind, which recognizes when a value matches a term already in your environment's controlled vocabulary, is built but not yet shown anywhere in the product. Maturity: Built — not yet available. Quiet-down for unhelpful tips — the platform can pause a kind of tip that researchers in an environment consistently pass over, so persistent noise switches itself off. This automatic pause is built but not yet running. Maturity: Built — not yet active. Aggregate-only usage figures — tip measurement, once running, records tip activity without naming the researcher, and figures about whether tips help are reported only in aggregate, withheld until enough activity contributes. Measurement is built but not yet collecting. Maturity: Built — not yet active.

You are editing a record or reviewing an import. A short note appears beside your work: one sentence of advice, with a brief reason underneath. Decide: Act on it. Make the edit it points to, the way you normally would. A tip is text — it carries no button and runs nothing on your behalf. Every change remains an edit you make yourself. Pass. Keep working. Nothing counts against you, and the tip goes away once it no longer applies — when the field is filled, or the review session moves on. That is the rhythm: small notes beside your work, yours to act on or pass over, never blocking.

You are editing a person record for Galen. Similar person records in your environment carry more detail on average, and this one has an empty birth-place field. An improvement tip surfaces, pointing out that records like this one usually have more fields filled and naming the birth place as a place to start. If the omission is deliberate — the birth place is genuinely unknown, or out of scope for your work — keep going. The tip does not insist, and it disappears once the comparison no longer holds. Later, you are reviewing an import and correct the same field the same way on a third row. An efficiency tip appears, noting that you have made the same correction several times. That is your cue to consider fixing the underlying mapping rule for the remaining rows instead of repeating the correction one row at a time.

When the review step of the import wizard is open, the tip panel sits beside the correction cards. Tips there fire only after a clear pattern — several corrections of the same shape within the session — and only when the platform is confident the suggestion is worth your attention. A blank panel during review is normal silence, not a fault.

Tips never change your data — there is no action a tip performs for you, so nothing happens without your own edit. Tips never penalize you for passing them over; ignored tips do not accumulate into a score or a warning. And tips never substitute for configuration — if your environment's required fields, vocabularies, or workflows are out of date, the right fix is to update the configuration, not to lean on tips. Raise that with your environment administrator.

Symptom Likely cause Fix A tip you expected never appears. The trigger was not met — too few similar records to compare against, no repeated correction pattern, or the suggestion was not confident enough to show. Tips may also be turned off for your environment. Confirm the trigger applies; an improvement tip needs at least three similar records in your environment. If tips seem off entirely, contact your environment administrator. The tip panel during import review is blank. No tip cleared the confidence bar for this session, or you have not yet repeated a correction enough times for a pattern to register. Nothing to fix — silence is intentional. A whole kind of tip stopped appearing. Tips were turned off for your environment, or that kind's trigger no longer applies to your records. If tips are gone everywhere, contact your environment administrator; otherwise there is nothing to fix. Tips feel noisy or distracting. The patterns in your data are triggering more suggestions than is helpful to you. Contact your environment administrator — tips can be turned off for the whole environment.

The workspace is the table of records of one type — figures, terms, manuscript editions, anything your project tracks — wrapped in a toolbar, a left sidebar, and a set of view tabs. This page walks through what is on the screen, what each control does, and what a typical session looks like. Read it when you first open the workspace, when a control is doing something you did not expect, or when you want to set up a view you can come back to.

Workspace layout (Active) — every table opens in the same shell: a left sidebar listing your tables, a top bar with search and the command palette, a toolbar of table controls, and view tabs that switch between Table, Details, Relations, and Publish. Workspace search (Active) — a quick search panel that finds records across the workspace, grouped by table. Results respect your permissions. When search cannot run, the panel says workspace search is unavailable rather than showing empty results. Search & Read section (Active) — a full search page with a typeahead, an advanced field-condition filter, paged results, and a reading pane that opens a record beside the list. The page address encodes the whole search, so it can be shared or bookmarked. Rows named by your display field (Active) — record labels in the table, the record panel, and search results use the display field your source declared, with a sensible fallback when none is declared. Sidebar organizer and command palette (Active) — pin tables, create named groups, collapse or expand groups, see your recently opened tables, and reset the sidebar to its defaults. The command palette reaches all of these without leaving the keyboard. Current-table quick filter (Active) — a toolbar box that narrows the rows already loaded in the active table. It is not a whole-workspace search. Filters (Active) — composable filter conditions per field. The filter options match the field's type: text fields offer contains and equals, numbers and dates offer ranges, choice fields offer their options, and linked-record fields let you search the linked table. Active filters appear as removable chips. Column manager (Active) — reorder, show or hide, and pin columns to the left or right; resize by dragging column edges in the table. Saved views (Active) — named tabs that remember filters, sort, column layout, density, and row colors. Views belong to the table and are shared with everyone who works in your environment. Per-view sharing permissions are not yet available. Density toggle (Active) — compact, cozy, or comfortable row height, remembered per view. Record panel (Active) — open any record to see every field with its editor, related records, and a preview of the saved public page. Fields composed from other fields are labeled read-only — they cannot be edited directly. Batch actions (Active) — select several rows to copy them to your clipboard or export them as a file. Buttons labeled "Backend pending" — such as batch delete and batch visibility — are visible but not yet available. Copy view link (Active) — copies a URL that opens the same view for a collaborator, subject to their own permissions.

Your knowledge environment has a sidebar listing the record types you can work with. Click one and you land in its workspace at /app/workspace/<record-type>/. You can bookmark and share the URL. If your project has several record types, each has its own workspace.

Find a record across the workspace. Click Search database… in the top bar, or press Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F. Type at least two characters. Choose Current table when you know the table, or All workspace when you do not — and in workspace scope you can still narrow to one table with the Table selector. Results are grouped by table; move with the arrow keys and press Enter, or click a result to open that record. The panel's Filter current table button hands your search words to the table's quick filter instead. When you want to browse and read many records at once, Open full Search & Read in the panel — or Search & Read in the command palette — opens the full search page, carrying your words over; see Searching and reading. Organize the left sidebar. Pin the tables you use most, gather tables into named groups, and collapse the groups you are not using. Recent lists the tables you opened last. Useful shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the command palette, Ctrl/Cmd+B collapses the sidebar to an icon rail, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G creates a group, and Shift+S pins or unpins the current table. Reset sidebar to default groups in the command palette puts everything back. Filter the table in front of you. Use the toolbar Filter visible rows box when you only need to narrow rows already loaded in the active table. This quick filter is transient and is not stored with the view. Add filters to narrow. Click Filter and pick a field. The options match the field's type — type a word for text fields, set a range for numbers and dates, pick options for choice fields, or search the linked table for linked-record fields. The match count updates as you set the condition. Filter chips appear in the toolbar after the "filtering by" lead-in. They compose. Remove a chip by clicking its ×; remove all of them with Clear. Tidy the columns. Click Columns to open the column manager: drag entries to reorder, uncheck columns to hide them, and pin a column to the left or right so it stays visible while scrolling. Resize a column by dragging its edge in the table itself. Save the arrangement as a view. Views are the tabs above the table. Click + Add view, give it a name like "18th-century figures with manuscript citations", and it starts from your current arrangement. From then on, changes you make while that view is active — filters, sort, columns, density — are stored on the view as you go. The toolbar's Undo and Redo step view changes backward and forward. Open a record. Click the row's Open details button (at the row's actions end) and the record panel opens over the table: every field with its editor, related records, and a preview of the saved public page. Close it with the × in its header, with Escape, or by clicking outside it. Edit in the table. Double-click a cell to edit it. Short values save when you press Enter or move away; larger editors — long text, formatted text — have their own Save and Cancel buttons. If a value cannot be saved, the workspace tells you rather than silently dropping it.
documents.s: The default flow: search, filter, open, edit

documents.t: Switch to the Details tab. It splits the screen: a list of the table's records on one side and the full record on the other. Click through the list and the record pane follows; the list can be narrowed with its own filter box, so you can audit a slice or fact-check a draft against its neighbors without losing your place.

Click a row to select it, Ctrl/Cmd+click to add or remove rows one at a time, and Shift+click to select a range. A batch toolbar appears showing the count. Copy selected puts the rows on your clipboard, ready to paste into a spreadsheet. Export selected downloads the selected records as a file. Buttons labeled "Backend pending" are not yet available. Clear the selection with the toolbar's × or with Escape.
Click Copy link in the toolbar, or Copy view link in a view tab's menu. Paste the URL into chat or email. Your collaborator opens it and lands on the same view, subject to their own permissions.
documents.s: Sharing a view with a collaborator

documents.t: A saved view remembers filters and their values, sort order, column layout (order, widths, pinning, hidden columns), row density, and row color rules. It does not remember the quick-filter text — that stays per-session so you do not accidentally land on yesterday's search. Views belong to the table, not to you alone: everyone working in your environment sees the same view tabs, and changes to a view reach your collaborators too. Each view's tab menu offers Rename, Duplicate, Pin view, Set as default (the view the table opens with), Copy view link, and Delete view. Deleting a view removes it for everyone, so agree with your collaborators first — Duplicate is the safe way to experiment on a shared view.

documents.t: Symptom Likely cause Fix Where to escalate A control mentioned here is missing or grayed out. The control depends on your role, or on a capability not yet available — grayed controls often say "Backend pending". Hover the control; its tooltip states the reason. Contact your environment administrator. Columns you arranged reverted later. The changes were made outside a saved view, so nothing stored them. Click + Add view, name it, and arrange columns while that view is active — changes then stick. n/a Search returns matches in an unexpected language or script form. The field stores several language or script forms, and search matches any of them. This is the intended behavior; see Searching and reading. Contact your environment administrator if matching is wrong for your project. The top search finds a row but the toolbar box does not. They are different tools: the top search looks across the workspace, while the toolbar box only filters rows already loaded in the current table. Open the result from the top search, or switch to the right table before using the toolbar filter. n/a The search panel says workspace search is unavailable. Your role does not include workspace search, or the search request failed. Try the search again; in the meantime, use the toolbar quick filter on the current table. Contact your environment administrator. Editing a cell does nothing. The field is read-only — composed fields, for example, cannot be edited directly — or the value was rejected. Open the record panel and check the field there; rejected values show a message instead of saving silently. Contact your environment administrator about permissions. The record panel will not close. A confirmation dialog is open and is catching the Escape key. Dismiss the dialog first, then press Escape. n/a
